sections.h2: Manistee County Register of Deeds office
sections.html:
The register works from the county courthouse at 415 Third Street, Manistee, MI 49660, and the phone is 231-723-2146. Weekday hours split around lunch: morning window 8:30 to noon, afternoon window 1 to 4. The Treasurer (231-723-3173) and Equalization Department (231-723-5957) share the street address and stay open until 5, so a seller can collect a deed certification and a parcel record in a single trip.

Manistee County had 25,032 residents at the 2020 census, and about 738 of its 1,281 square miles are Lake Michigan water, so shoreline and lake property drive much of the market. Manistee is the only city and the seat.

Staff keep the records but will not run title for anyone. The office makes simple searches that reach back 20 years and sends anyone needing a full title search to a title company. A document handed in goes through a seven step recordation process, which usually takes one to two business days.

You do not have to come to the courthouse. Mailing completed documents to Register of Deeds, 415 3rd Street, Manistee, MI 49660 is acceptable and legal in almost every situation. Call 231-723-2146 first if you want the cost confirmed. The office accepts every form of payment, and it returns copies to other parties once copy fees are paid and an addressed, stamped envelope is supplied.

Manistee's business rules for electronic filers are:

  • Documents are handled between 8:30 a.m. and 2:30 p.m. on weekdays, holidays excepted.
  • Payment goes through ACH, under each vendor's agreement.
  • A vendor that submits documents breaking the Michigan eRecording Standards can lose submission access.
  • The register may reject an electronic document that fails the recording act.
  • Changes to these rules are posted 90 days before they take effect.

The vendors may charge their own processing fees, but the register itself collects only the fees written into law.

The flat recording charge is $30, with a $3 extra for each additional instrument released in one document. Copy pricing has its own shape here: $7 buys a two page real estate record copy and each added page is $1. The office requires payment before it releases anything.

Online access is a pay for view site covering 1978 forward, and a separate search tool covers 1856 through 1991. The vault is open to the public for those who prefer to dig through the books.

When you order copies, bring a list of the instruments you need. Budget for the certification fee if a title company or lender wants a certified version, and ask the office to confirm the total before you pay, since payment comes first.

sections.h2: Why a warranty deed goes to the Treasurer first
sections.html:
Manistee's routing is unusual. You hand a warranty deed, a land contract, an assignment with a warranty clause or a condominium master deed to the County Treasurer for certification, and the Treasurer forwards it to the register with the fees. The register sends nothing back to the Treasurer, and an uncertified instrument is returned to whoever sent it. The legal basis is MCL 211.135, and the certificate costs $5.

The Treasurer's office also keeps tax histories on real property, handles Principal Residence Exemption audits, and bills or refunds for board of review changes. That makes it the right stop for a payoff question. A quitclaim deed with no warranty covenant needs no certificate.

Each year, summer bills go out July 1. City summer taxes are due August 20, township and village summer taxes September 14, and winter taxes February 14. Unpaid township and city taxes move to the County Treasurer on March 1 with a 4% fee and 1% monthly interest, and foreclosure follows about three years after the tax year.

For a sale, give the title company the parcel details early and ask them to send the warranty deed to the Treasurer rather than straight to the register. That one routing step avoids a returned document and a delay at closing.

sections.h2: How a tax foreclosure plays out
sections.html:
After forfeiture on March 1 of the second year, the county's timeline stacks on several charges:

  • $175 for the title search, $60 for recording and $7.10 for notice.
  • Interest at 1.5% a month, applied back to the prior year.
  • $45 for a site inspection in June.
  • $50 for publication in December.

Notice runs in the Manistee News Advocate twice in January, and the Treasurer holds a show cause hearing. The circuit court enters judgment in February. Taxes can be paid through March 31 of the third year, and foreclosure becomes final the next day.

Tax-foreclosed property in the county goes to an online auction run by a contractor, Title Check, LLC. The auction happens once a year, typically in August or September. It opens with a minimum bid round, then a re-offer round with sealed bids, then a no reserve round with sealed bids about a month apart.

A former owner can file a Notice of Intention to Claim Interest in Foreclosure Sales Proceeds (Form 5743), due July 1 in the foreclosure year, and later a court motion to claim remaining proceeds. A seller with unpaid taxes should settle them before forfeiture, while a normal sale is still possible.

sections.h2: Property tax and transfer tax after a sale
sections.html:
The Equalization Department keeps the tax rolls up to date for transfers, principal residence and agricultural exemptions, and uncapping. It sets no individual assessment, since its role is to survey classes of property across the city and townships. Under MCL 211.27a, a transfer of ownership lifts taxable value to the state equalized value for the following year, so a buyer's first bill can exceed what the seller paid. The buyer reports the transfer to the local assessor within 45 days.

Transfer tax is separate and falls on the seller. The rate is $0.55 per $500 for the county and $3.75 per $500 for the state, with a $100 floor. Check the legislature's exemption lists for transfers that owe nothing, such as family transfers of the kinds those lists cover.

Confirm the exemption wording with your title company before the deed is signed, since an exemption has to be claimed on the document.

faqs.q: What is the total cost to file a warranty deed in Manistee County?
faqs.a: Plan on $35, which is the $30 recording charge plus the $5 treasurer certification. A document that releases several instruments adds $3 for each one after the first.

faqs.q: When is the Manistee County register office closed during the day?
faqs.a: The lunch hour, noon to 1 p.m., is the gap. Doors are open for the morning and afternoon windows, weekdays only.

faqs.q: Can Manistee County staff run a title for my house?
faqs.a: Staff can do simple searches back 20 years, but they will not run a full title. For that you need a title company, and the office cannot give legal advice.

faqs.q: How is the Manistee County tax auction run?
faqs.a: It is online and held once a year, usually in August or September, through Title Check, LLC. It has a minimum bid round followed by re-offer and no reserve rounds.

faqs.q: What transfer tax applies to a Manistee County sale?
faqs.a: The county charges $0.55 per $500 and the state charges $3.75 per $500. The seller owes it unless the deed is exempt.
